title: Dates, Times and Date-Time Groups
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapters 2 and 4
notes: Conventions for expressing dates, time and DTGs in Service writing.

rules.title: Dates are written day, month, year
rules.description: A date is to be written in the order: day, month, year.

rules.title: Abbreviated dates use 3-letter month and 2-figure year
rules.description: An abbreviated date uses the first 3 letters of the month followed by the last 2 figures of the year, with cardinal numbers for the day, e.g. '1 Jul 23'.

rules.title: Nights are described by both dates over which they extend
rules.description: A night is described by both dates over which it extends, e.g. 'night 29/30 Sep' or 'night 30 Sep/1 Oct'.

rules.title: Time is expressed on the 24-hour clock in four figures
rules.description: Time is expressed in 4 figures by reference to the 24-hour clock; the first pair of figures indicates the hour and the second pair the minutes.

rules.title: The 12-hour clock with am/pm is never used in Defence writing
rules.description: While never used in Defence writing, time expressed in terms of the 12-hour clock followed by 'am' or 'pm' is normal in dealings with civilians and social invitations.

rules.title: The term 'midnight' is not used; use '0000 hours'
rules.description: The term 'midnight' is not used when referring to that precise time; '0000 hours' and the date are used instead.

rules.title: DTGs consist of 6 figures, zone suffix, 3-letter month and 2-figure year
rules.description: DTGs are used to give the date and time of origin of signal messages and certain orders; they consist of 6 figures, the first 2 giving the day of the month and the last 4 the time, followed by a time zone suffix, the first 3 letters of the month in capitals and the last 2 digits of the year, e.g. 221415C Aug 20.

check.where: DTG references in text and messages.

rules.title: A year on its own is always written in full
rules.description: Where a year appears on its own, it is always to be written in full, e.g. 2013, not 13.
rules.notes: Heuristic: flags standalone two-digit numbers that may be intended as years; requires human confirmation.
